Subject: Feature parity: streaming & tool calling - next tests

Thanks again for a great call today \u00150 appreciate the clarity on Acme's streaming and structured-output use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a focused comparison against the hyperscalers you mentioned.

Recap:
- Primary goals: 1) end-to-end streaming latency for 200-500 token responses, 2) reliable function/tool calling with structured JSON outputs, 3) model behavior parity on our prompt suite (intent extraction + multi-step tool calls).
- Success criteria: median streaming latency < 300ms token-to-token for typical user flows, function call accuracy > 92% on structured fields, and no regressions on follow-up prompts.

Proposed next tests (attached test plan):
- Streaming latency sweep (short/medium/long contexts) \u00150 run against Redwood hosted endpoint + Hyperscaler A and Hyperscaler B.
- Tool/function call harness \u00150 our harness will hit: 1) single tool call, 2) multi-tool sequence (2-3 calls), 3) nested tool response parsing. Capture structured-json fidelity and error rates.
- Structured output & schema enforcement \u00150 check strictness of returned JSON and edge-case handling.

Action items I can own from Redwood:
1) Provision test endpoints and short-lived API keys for Acme (will send creds + network details).
2) Provide the harness and a matched prompt suite (see attached CSV).
3) Run an initial 2-hour smoke test and share logs + token/latency breakdowns.

Can you confirm the people who should get the test creds and whether we should run tests in us-west1 only or across multi-region (we can mirror to eu if needed)? Also propose a 45-min technical sync this week to walk through the harness and the initial results.

Attachments: acme-feature-parity-test-plan.csv (test matrix), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-summary.pdf (short differentiator doc)

Thanks,
